chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the slaughter of the boy and the woman, can it be eaten? So he (peace be upon him) said: When the woman is a Muslim, and she mentions the Name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon her slaughter, her slaughter becomes permissible, and similarly the boy, when he is strong enough for the slaughter, and mentions the Name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, over it, and that is when there is fear of losing the slaughtered animal, and there is no one else to slaughter it.
ai.seo_question: Is the slaughter of a child or woman permissible in Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq) to clarify the conditions under which a child or woman can validly perform dhabihah in emergencies, such as when the meat is at risk of spoilage and no other adult is available. The ruling hinges on the individual being Muslim, reciting the name of Allah, and possessing sufficient physical capability to slaughter, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of extending ritual validity to those with minimal capacity in dire circumstances. This highlights the flexibility of Shia fiqh in preserving sustenance while maintaining ritual purity.
